## doxyguard-db
Queryable knowledge database over a doxygen-guard-enforced C/C++ or Python codebase.

WHAT THIS IS FOR. The index holds a repository's symbols, call relationships, threads, locks and
critical sections, dispatch, requirement links, file inventory and prose. It answers structural
questions about a symbol and its neighbours in one call where reading source takes several. It is
NOT a replacement for reading source: a question about how one name is spelled differently for
different consumers, or about the exact text of a comment, is one the index can point at but not
settle. Reading source after the index has named the file is the intended path, not a failure.

NO PERFORMANCE FIGURES ARE QUOTED HERE, deliberately. This text is served to a model that is
sometimes then graded on the answers it gives, so a number here describing which question types
the index wins teaches to the test and quietly turns a benchmark into a self-portrait. Measured
results live in the repository's committed acceptance artifacts, where a reader can check them
against the transcripts they came from.

ONE SERVER ANSWERS ABOUT ANY INDEXED REPOSITORY. Every tool takes an optional `target` — a repo
root path, or a slug. Pass it and that repository answers; omit it and the DEFAULT target answers.
The server keeps nothing between calls, so a `target` on one call never changes what the next one
sees.

The default target is DERIVED, not set: from --repo, else $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR. There is no
set_target tool. Administration is ONE tool with an `action`: `index(action='targets')` lists every
indexed repository, `index(action='refresh')` builds or updates one, `index(action='status')` gives

7	`build_index` five more, so through MCP the built-in defaults WERE the whole policy. A
8	five-tier precedence rule whose top tier no consumer can reach makes tier 5 the ceiling
9	rather than the floor.
10	
11	THE VOCABULARY IS THE DECLARATION FILE'S. An operator who learns `shared_key_patterns`
12	here has learned the key they would write into `.doxyguard-db.yaml`, and the diagnostics
13	(gh#320) name their findings in the same words. That closes the loop: the tool says what
14	it could not see, in the vocabulary you use to tell it.
15	
16	AND IT IS NOW 14 OF 14, MEASURED — every declaration section is statable, with the one
17	remaining ASYMMETRY named rather than left to be discovered (gh#382).
18	`test_every_declaration_section_has_a_matching_option` asserts the difference in both
19	directions, so a new section arrives with an option or breaks a test:
20	
21	  * `predefined` is an option with no SECTION, kept as a documented alias for
22	    `preprocessor.predefined`: the acceptance harness and every existing caller name it, and
23	    a bare macro list is the common case. The section form is what can also state
24	    `config_header:`, which the alias cannot express at all.
25	
26	THE COUNT MOVED 11 → 13 BECAUSE THE CLI COLLAPSED, NOT BECAUSE TWO FEATURES WERE ADDED.
27	`requirements` and `enrich` were argparse flags with no declaration home at all: statable
28	only by an operator with a shell, which is the exact shape this module's own reasoning below
29	rejects for the caller it exists for. Folding the 22-argument build surface to 6 made them
30	sections and options like everything else, so the sentence "the option name is the section
31	name" now has no exceptions but the documented `predefined` alias.
32	
33	`doxyfile` IS THE FOURTEENTH, AND IT REVERSES A CLAIM THIS DOCSTRING USED TO MAKE (gh#420).
34	The paragraph below listed `--doxyfile` beside `--scope`, `--index-cache` and `--rebuild` as
35	build MECHANICS that "have no section and never should". That was wrong about this one, and
36	the counter-example was already in this module: `kconfig:` is a section for exactly the same
37	reason — its discovery follows a convention, and a repo whose file sits outside that
38	convention needs a way to SAY so. Where a repository keeps its own documentation target is a
39	standing property of that repository, not a fact about one run.
40	
41	Measured: `discover_doxyfile` matches the NAME `Doxyfile` in the root, `docs/` and `doc/` and
42	refuses to guess beyond it — it was once caught selecting a test FIXTURE's Doxyfile to index a
43	whole project. Mbed-TLS ships `doxygen/mbedtls.doxyfile`, wrong directory AND wrong filename,
44	so `scope.doxyfile_*` stayed EMPTY on the one acceptance target whose rubric asks about it
45	while `_doxyfile_scope` sat fully built and unreachable. `--doxyfile` could name it on one
46	command line, which is precisely the shape the mandate calls not-a-declaration: unrecorded,
47	unreplayed, and invisible from the MCP surface.
48	
49	Stating it does NOT choose what gets indexed — since gh#333 a Doxyfile's INPUT, EXCLUDE* and
50	FILE_PATTERNS are all replaced — so the reversal costs nothing in scope semantics. And unlike
51	every other path option it must EXIST when stated (`PATH_OPTIONS_MUST_EXIST`), because
52	resolution otherwise falls through to whole-repo synthesis, which is a legitimate build: the
53	result would be a well-formed index of a different thing, reporting success.
54	
55	WHAT DID *NOT* BECOME A DECLARATION, and the distinction is worth stating because it is the
56	one a reader will test this claim against. `--scope`, `--index-cache` and
57	`--rebuild` are build MECHANICS — facts about one run, not about the repository — so they
58	have no section and never should. `--guard-config` was DELETED in favour of discovery rather
59	than folded, because `discover_guard_config` already finds it from the repo root alone and
60	carrying a declaration is what `--declare` now does directly. `--verbose` changes the CLI's
61	own stderr and nothing that reaches the index.
62	
63	`index_scope` was the last gap and took its own route rather than the merge. It is resolved by
64	`derive_scope_logged` BEFORE the declaration the stages read is loaded, so the injection point
65	below cannot reach it; the stated document is threaded down to `scope._declared_index_scope`
66	instead and built through the SAME construction a written one takes. Only the reported `reason`

571	    `entry.get("name")` returning None and the loader skipping the entry silently.
572	
573	    @brief Check one manifest list's entries.
574	    @version 1
575	    """
576	    entries = document.get(schema.list_key)
577	    if entries is None:
578	        return
579	    if not isinstance(entries, list):
580	        raise BuildOptionError(
581	            f"option {key!r}: {schema.list_key!r} must be a list of entries, got "
582	            f"{type(entries).__name__}"
583	        )
584	    for position, entry in enumerate(entries, start=1):
585	        _checked_entry(key, f"{schema.list_key}[{position}]", entry, schema)
586	
587	
588	## @brief Validate one entry mapping against its schema.
589	## @param key The option name, for the message.
590	## @param where Which list and position the entry sits at.
591	## @param entry The entry supplied.
592	## @param schema The entry schema.
593	## @return None; raises when the entry is shaped wrongly.
594	## @version 1
595	## @dg_internal
596	def _checked_entry(key: str, where: str, entry: Any, schema: EntrySchema) -> None:
597	    """@brief Check one manifest entry's keys against the allowed and required sets.
598	    @version 1
599	    """
600	    if not isinstance(entry, dict):
601	        raise BuildOptionError(
602	            f"option {key!r}: {where} must be a mapping, got {type(entry).__name__}"
603	        )
604	    unknown = sorted(str(k) for k in entry if k not in schema.allowed)
605	    if unknown:
606	        raise BuildOptionError(
607	            f"option {key!r}: {where} names unknown key(s) "
608	            f"{', '.join(repr(k) for k in unknown)} — allowed: "
609	            f"{', '.join(sorted(schema.allowed))}. A misspelled field reads as an absent "
610	            f"one, so it would silently take its default."
611	        )
612	    missing = [name for name in schema.required if not entry.get(name)]
613	    if missing:
614	        raise BuildOptionError(
615	            f"option {key!r}: {where} is missing required key(s) "
616	            f"{', '.join(repr(m) for m in missing)}"
617	        )
618	    if schema.any_of and not any(entry.get(name) for name in schema.any_of):
619	        raise BuildOptionError(
620	            f"option {key!r}: {where} declares none of "
621	            f"{', '.join(repr(name) for name in schema.any_of)} — it would match nothing"
622	        )
623	
624	
625	## @brief Resolve one manifest option, which may be a path or the document inline.
626	## @param key The option name, for the message.
627	## @param value A path string/Path, or the manifest document as a mapping.
628	## @param repo_root Root to resolve a relative path against, or None.
629	## @return An absolute path string, or the validated mapping.
630	## @version 1
631	## @dg_internal
632	def _checked_manifest(key: str, value: Any, repo_root: Path | None) -> str | dict[str, Any]:
633	    """BOTH FORMS REACH THE SAME PARSER. Every loader behind these options already accepts
634	    `Path | dict`, because a `.doxyguard-db.yaml` section arrives as a mapping — so the
635	    inline form adds a route, not a format, and `treescan.manifest_key` hashes a mapping
636	    canonically, which is what keeps gh#358's per-stage cache invalidation intact: stating
637	    one manifest recomputes the stages that manifest feeds and no others.
638	
639	    @brief Resolve a manifest option from either input form.
640	    @return Path string or validated document.
641	    @version 1
642	    """
643	    if isinstance(value, dict):
644	        return _checked_document(key, value)
645	    if not isinstance(value, (str, Path)):
646	        raise BuildOptionError(
647	            f"option {key!r} must be a path to a YAML document, or that document inline "
648	            f"as a mapping, got {type(value).__name__}"
649	        )
650	    return _checked_path(key, value, repo_root)
651	
652	
653	## @brief Apply a validated options mapping onto a parsed argument namespace.
654	## @param args Namespace from the build argument parser, mutated in place.
655	## @param options Caller-stated options, or None to change nothing.
656	## @param repo_root Root that relative path options resolve against.
657	## @return The names actually applied, sorted, for logging.
658	## @version 3
659	## @req REQ-DDB-CONFIG-008
660	def apply_options(args: Any, options: dict[str, Any] | None, repo_root: Path | None) -> list[str]:
661	    """VALIDATES EVERYTHING BEFORE ASSIGNING ANYTHING, so a mapping with one bad entry
662	    leaves the namespace untouched rather than half-applied. A partially-applied policy
663	    would build with a mixture of what the caller asked for and what they did not, and
664	    report success — the same class of defect as a partially-reloaded pipeline.
665	
666	    `None` and `{}` both change nothing, and neither is an error: a caller that forwards
667	    its own optional argument gets the inheriting behaviour by default. An empty document
668	    for ONE manifest option (`shared_key_patterns: {}`) is the per-option equivalent — it
669	    states nothing, so that manifest falls back to the target's own declaration, matching
670	    the absent/empty/replaces convention `--exclude` and `--entry-patterns` already keep.
671	
672	    @brief Validate and apply tier-1 options.
673	    @return Applied option names.
674	    @version 2
675	    """
676	    if not options:
677	        return []
678	    if not isinstance(options, dict):
679	        raise BuildOptionError(f"options must be a mapping, got {type(options).__name__}")
680	    staged: dict[str, Any] = {}
681	    for key, value in options.items():
682	        if key in INLINE_LIST_OPTIONS:
683	            staged[key] = _checked_list(key, value)
684	        elif key in INLINE_MAPPING_OPTIONS:
685	            staged[key] = _checked_mapping(key, value)
686	        elif key in MANIFEST_OPTIONS:
687	            staged[key] = _checked_manifest(key, value, repo_root)
688	        elif key in PATH_OPTIONS:
689	            staged[key] = _checked_path(key, value, repo_root)
690	        elif key in SECTION_DOCUMENT_OPTIONS:
691	            staged[key] = _checked_section_document(key, value)
692	        else:
693	            _refuse(key)
694	    for key, value in staged.items():
695	        setattr(args, key, value)
696	    return sorted(staged)

# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
"""TIER 1, REACHABLE — one structured `options` argument for an embedding caller.

`.doxyguard-db.yaml` is TIER 2 and has been reachable since a declaration became
discoverable from `--repo-root`. Tier 1 — an operator STATING a value at call time —
never was: `build_or_refresh` exposed `force`/`doxyfile`/`scope`/`exclude`/`target`, and
`build_index` five more, so through MCP the built-in defaults WERE the whole policy. A
five-tier precedence rule whose top tier no consumer can reach makes tier 5 the ceiling
rather than the floor.

THE VOCABULARY IS THE DECLARATION FILE'S. An operator who learns `shared_key_patterns`
here has learned the key they would write into `.doxyguard-db.yaml`, and the diagnostics
(gh#320) name their findings in the same words. That closes the loop: the tool says what
it could not see, in the vocabulary you use to tell it.

AND IT IS NOW 14 OF 14, MEASURED — every declaration section is statable, with the one
remaining ASYMMETRY named rather than left to be discovered (gh#382).
`test_every_declaration_section_has_a_matching_option` asserts the difference in both
directions, so a new section arrives with an option or breaks a test:

  * `predefined` is an option with no SECTION, kept as a documented alias for
    `preprocessor.predefined`: the acceptance harness and every existing caller name it, and
    a bare macro list is the common case. The section form is what can also state
    `config_header:`, which the alias cannot express at all.

THE COUNT MOVED 11 → 13 BECAUSE THE CLI COLLAPSED, NOT BECAUSE TWO FEATURES WERE ADDED.
`requirements` and `enrich` were argparse flags with no declaration home at all: statable
only by an operator with a shell, which is the exact shape this module's own reasoning below
rejects for the caller it exists for. Folding the 22-argument build surface to 6 made them
sections and options like everything else, so the sentence "the option name is the section
name" now has no exceptions but the documented `predefined` alias.

`doxyfile` IS THE FOURTEENTH, AND IT REVERSES A CLAIM THIS DOCSTRING USED TO MAKE (gh#420).
The paragraph below listed `--doxyfile` beside `--scope`, `--index-cache` and `--rebuild` as
build MECHANICS that "have no section and never should". That was wrong about this one, and
the counter-example was already in this module: `kconfig:` is a section for exactly the same
reason — its discovery follows a convention, and a repo whose file sits outside that
convention needs a way to SAY so. Where a repository keeps its own documentation target is a
standing property of that repository, not a fact about one run.

Measured: `discover_doxyfile` matches the NAME `Doxyfile` in the root, `docs/` and `doc/` and
refuses to guess beyond it — it was once caught selecting a test FIXTURE's Doxyfile to index a
whole project. Mbed-TLS ships `doxygen/mbedtls.doxyfile`, wrong directory AND wrong filename,
so `scope.doxyfile_*` stayed EMPTY on the one acceptance target whose rubric asks about it
while `_doxyfile_scope` sat fully built and unreachable. `--doxyfile` could name it on one
command line, which is precisely the shape the mandate calls not-a-declaration: unrecorded,
unreplayed, and invisible from the MCP surface.

Stating it does NOT choose what gets indexed — since gh#333 a Doxyfile's INPUT, EXCLUDE* and
FILE_PATTERNS are all replaced — so the reversal costs nothing in scope semantics. And unlike
every other path option it must EXIST when stated (`PATH_OPTIONS_MUST_EXIST`), because
resolution otherwise falls through to whole-repo synthesis, which is a legitimate build: the
result would be a well-formed index of a different thing, reporting success.

WHAT DID *NOT* BECOME A DECLARATION, and the distinction is worth stating because it is the
one a reader will test this claim against. `--scope`, `--index-cache` and
`--rebuild` are build MECHANICS — facts about one run, not about the repository — so they
have no section and never should. `--guard-config` was DELETED in favour of discovery rather
than folded, because `discover_guard_config` already finds it from the repo root alone and
carrying a declaration is what `--declare` now does directly. `--verbose` changes the CLI's
own stderr and nothing that reaches the index.

`index_scope` was the last gap and took its own route rather than the merge. It is resolved by
`derive_scope_logged` BEFORE the declaration the stages read is loaded, so the injection point
below cannot reach it; the stated document is threaded down to `scope._declared_index_scope`
instead and built through the SAME construction a written one takes. Only the reported `reason`
differs — it says "stated by the caller (tier 1)" rather than naming a file — and it must, or an
owner would go and edit a file that says nothing. Pairing a stated `index_scope` with any
`--scope` other than `from-guard` REFUSES, because that path never reads it and would build a
different boundary while reporting success.

Before gh#382 the two unreachable sections were `preprocessor` and `kconfig`, and the plan
that scheduled this work named neither correctly — it listed `config_header`, which is a KEY
INSIDE `preprocessor` rather than a section of its own. Counting them was one query; the
list in the plan was three items and two of them were wrong.

TWO CONVENTIONS IN ONE ARGUMENT, deliberately (owner decision, 2026-08-10):

  * INLINE for the values that are a list or a small mapping. `event_tags` is the case
    that proves the need — it has no CLI flag at all, by an explicit earlier decision
    that a bus vocabulary is a standing property of a repo, so before this there was no
    route to state it other than editing the target's own tree.
  * BY PATH for the six manifest-shaped documents. Every loader takes a `Path`; giving
    each a second input type to save an operator a file is a poor trade, and a recorded
    path is reproducible where a recorded structure is a frozen copy.

THAT SECOND BULLET IS REVERSED (gh#360, owner decision 2026-08-11) AND THE REASONING
ABOVE IS KEPT RATHER THAN DELETED, because it is still correct about the case it was
about: AN OPERATOR WITH A SHELL. For them a path IS the better input — reproducible,
diffable, and already written down. It does not hold for the caller this surface exists
for. An AGENT mid-session has no shell and must not write into the target: a third-party
repo stays byte-identical, so `.doxyguard-db.yaml` is unavailable, and a YAML file at some
absolute path outside the tree is untracked, unreproducible, and deleted by the acceptance
harness's own `git clean`. "Save an operator a file" was never the trade; the trade is
whether a declaration is REACHABLE at all from a caller with no filesystem to write to —
the same shape as the recorded lesson that a declaration reachable only from argv is not a
declaration. So each manifest option now accepts EITHER form, and the path form is
untouched: an operator's recorded path keeps being a recorded path.

THE INLINE FORM IS VALIDATED HARDER THAN THE FILE FORM, and that asymmetry is deliberate.
`MANIFEST_SCHEMAS` below refuses an unknown key at the ENTRY level, which is the level
this repo has recorded as the quiet one: `key_arg_idx` for `key_arg_index` parses to a
perfectly valid mapping, every loader reads the misspelling as absent, and the dataflow is
then keyed off argument 0 with the build reporting success. The loaders' own `entry.get(…,
default)` cannot see that, and tightening them would change what an existing target's
committed declaration means — a separate decision, not this one's to make. Stricter on the
new route costs an author one error message; laxer on it would have shipped the defect.

FAIL CLOSED AT BOTH LEVELS, because the quieter one is the entry level. A misspelled
SECTION is refused by name against the allowed set — the `load_declaration_located`
precedent. But `{"broadcasts": "produce"}` for `producer` would parse as a perfectly valid
mapping that no consumer reads, silently leaving the bus undeclared while the call
reported success. So role values are checked against the vocabulary too.

@brief Validate and apply an embedding caller's tier-1 build options.
@version 5
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

from .event_edges import CONSUMER, PRODUCER

## Keys whose value is a LIST OF STRINGS, applied inline. Each names an argparse dest that
## already exists, so a stated value lands exactly where the equivalent flag would.
## `vendored` is a plain list of repo-relative paths, exactly the shape `entry_patterns` is,
## so it rides the same inline route. It has to be statable at TIER 1 for the case it exists
## for: a third-party target whose tree must stay byte-identical cannot carry a
## `.doxyguard-db.yaml`, so an agent or an acceptance harness states it on the call.
INLINE_LIST_OPTIONS: tuple[str, ...] = ("entry_patterns", "predefined", "vendored")

## Keys whose value is a MAPPING, applied inline. `event_tags` maps a tag name to a role.
INLINE_MAPPING_OPTIONS: tuple[str, ...] = ("event_tags",)

## Keys whose value is a PATH and only ever a path.
##
## `data_model` is the one MANIFEST that is NOT YAML — an ingot/UDM TOML document, named by
## a repo-relative path in the declaration too — so there is no equivalent inline structure
## to accept.
##
## `requirements` and `enrich` are here because a path is ALL either one ever was: each
## names a document in the target's own tree whose format belongs to that repo, not to this
## tool. There is deliberately no inline form. A requirements catalog has no universal shape
## (this repo's own rule: "there is NO universal requirements.yaml format", one flat list and
## one nested `domains:` tree, read additively), so accepting one inline would mean this
## module choosing a shape the mandate forbids it to assume. Same for an enrichment topics
## document. Both were CLI flags with no declaration home, which is why a repo could not
## state either one through the surface an agent uses.
##
## `doxyfile` joins them for gh#420, and it is the one whose absence changes WHICH SOURCE is
## indexed rather than which metadata is attached. `discover_doxyfile` matches the NAME
## `Doxyfile` in the repo root, `docs/` and `doc/`, and REFUSES to guess beyond that — it once
## took `sorted(repo.glob("*/Doxyfile"))[0]` and selected a test FIXTURE's Doxyfile to index a
## whole project. Mbed-TLS/mbedtls ships `doxygen/mbedtls.doxyfile`: wrong directory AND wrong
## filename, so no discovery reaches it and, before this key, nothing could state it either.
## Widening the glob would trade a fixable gap for an unfixable class of wrong answer; a
## DECLARATION is the answer the no-hardcoding mandate already prescribes.
PATH_OPTIONS: tuple[str, ...] = ("data_model", "requirements", "enrich", "doxyfile")

## Of the path options, the ones whose stated path must EXIST when it is stated.
##
## THE DISTINCTION IS METADATA VERSUS FILE SET, not caution. A missing `requirements` catalog
## degrades to empty metadata over the same rows — honest, recoverable, and each loader says so
## in its own words, which is why `_checked_path` deliberately does not check existence. A
## missing `doxyfile` changes WHICH SOURCE IS COMPILED INTO THE INDEX: resolution falls through
## to whole-repo synthesis, which is a legitimate build, so the result is a well-formed index of
## a different thing. `_resolve_doxyfile_and_root` warns in that case and is deliberately
## non-fatal for the `--doxyfile` FLAG (`--repo-root` alone is sufficient), and a warning is
## exactly what this project has repeatedly found to be gone by query time.
##
## So the refusal lives at the boundary where the DECLARATION is made, matching the entry-level
## rule this repo learned the hard way: a document-level slip is loud, and an entry-level one is
## quiet enough to build green and be believed.
PATH_OPTIONS_MUST_EXIST: frozenset[str] = frozenset({"doxyfile"})

## Keys accepting EITHER a path to a YAML document OR that document inline (gh#360). Every
## loader behind these already takes `Path | dict`, because a `.doxyguard-db.yaml` section
## arrives as a mapping — so the inline form needs no new parser, only a validated route in.
MANIFEST_OPTIONS: tuple[str, ...] = (
    "shared_key_patterns",
    "thread_patterns",
    "locks",
    "dispatch",
    "mqtt_dispatch",
)

## Keys naming a DECLARATION SECTION whose whole document is stated inline (gh#382). These
## have NO argparse dest and never did — they were tier-2 only, readable from a checked-in
## `.doxyguard-db.yaml` and unreachable from the MCP surface, which is the exact shape
## CLAUDE.md forbids: "a declaration reachable only from argv is not a declaration", read the
## other way round.
##
## THE OPTION NAME IS THE SECTION NAME, which is the owner's 1:1 ruling made literal. They are
## applied by MERGING INTO THE DECLARATION the stages already read, rather than by adding three
## more dests and three more resolution orders — one injection point, and every consumer of
## `decl` gets the stated value for free.
##
## `predefined` REMAINS as a convenience alias for `preprocessor.predefined` because the
## acceptance harness and every existing caller name it, and because a bare macro list is the
## common case. It is the one option whose name is not a section, and it is documented as such
## rather than quietly tolerated.
SECTION_DOCUMENT_OPTIONS: tuple[str, ...] = ("preprocessor", "kconfig", "index_scope")


## @brief One list-of-entries key inside a manifest, and the keys its entries may carry.
## @version 1
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class EntrySchema:
    """The ENTRY-LEVEL allow-list, which is the level the loaders cannot police for
    themselves. Every one of them reads its fields with `entry.get(name, default)`, so a
    misspelled field is indistinguishable from an omitted one and silently takes the
    default — `key_arg_idx` keys a whole dataflow layer off argument 0.

    `any_of` rather than `required` where a shape is a genuine either/or: a shared-key
    entry is the argument-based convention (`pattern`) or the name-based one
    (`name_prefix`), never both and never neither.

    @brief Allowed and required keys for one manifest list's entries.
    @version 1
    """

    list_key: str
    allowed: frozenset[str]
    required: tuple[str, ...] = ()
    any_of: tuple[str, ...] = field(default_factory=tuple)


## @brief One inline manifest's whole shape: its top-level keys and its entry lists.
## @version 1
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ManifestSchema:
    """`document` is the DOCUMENT-level allow-list and is not derivable from `entries`:
    `shared_key_patterns` legitimately carries a `key_alias_prefixes` list of strings
    beside its two entry lists, so deriving the allowed set from the entry schemas would
    refuse a correct declaration. Two levels, stated separately, matching
    `declaration.KNOWN_SECTIONS` above them and `dispatch._reject_unknown` beside them.

    @brief The allowed shape of one inline manifest.
    @version 1
    """

    document: frozenset[str]
    entries: tuple[EntrySchema, ...]


## What an inline manifest may contain, per option. The KEYS ARE THIS PROJECT'S OWN
## FORMAT, not any target's convention, so writing them down here is not the hardcoding
## the mandate forbids — it is the same document-level allow-list `declaration.py` keeps
## for section names, one level in.
##
## `dispatch` IS ABSENT ON PURPOSE and validated by `load_dispatch_manifest`, which already
## refuses an unknown key at the document level AND in each of its three entry shapes
## (`dispatch._reject_unknown`). Restating its schema here would be a second copy free to
## drift from the parser that reads it; no schema means "its own loader is stricter than
## anything this module would write", and `_checked_manifest` says so rather than treating
## the absence as permission to skip checking.
MANIFEST_SCHEMAS: dict[str, ManifestSchema] = {
    "shared_key_patterns": ManifestSchema(
        document=frozenset({"writers", "readers", "key_alias_prefixes"}),
        entries=(
            EntrySchema(
                "writers",
                frozenset({"pattern", "key_arg_index", "name_prefix", "dispatch_mode"}),
                any_of=("pattern", "name_prefix"),
            ),
            EntrySchema(
                "readers",
                frozenset({"pattern", "key_arg_index", "name_prefix", "dispatch_mode"}),
                any_of=("pattern", "name_prefix"),
            ),
        ),
    ),
    "thread_patterns": ManifestSchema(
        document=frozenset({"spawns"}),
        entries=(
            EntrySchema(
                "spawns",
                frozenset(
                    {
                        "name",
                        "entry_arg_index",
                        "name_arg_index",
                        "kind",
                        "entry_kwarg",
                        "name_kwarg",
                    }
                ),
                required=("name",),
            ),
        ),
    ),
    "locks": ManifestSchema(
        document=frozenset({"locks"}),
        entries=(
            EntrySchema(
                "locks",
                ## `releases` WAS MISSING, and it is the one key a call-form primitive cannot
                ## work without. `locks._declared_lock_pattern` has always read it, so the same
                ## declaration was accepted from a `.doxyguard-db.yaml` file and REFUSED here —
                ## two documents disagreeing about one fact, which is the third instance of that
                ## shape in this area (see #404's three-way disagreement and #407's prompt vs
                ## parser). Without a release token `_section_for` finds nothing to close the
                ## extent, so every critical section stays NULL: the declaration that makes
                ## mbedtls's 48 lock sites harvestable was exactly the one this route rejected.
                frozenset({"name", "form", "kind", "mode", "role", "operand_index", "releases"}),
                required=("name",),
            ),
        ),
    ),
    "mqtt_dispatch": ManifestSchema(
        document=frozenset({"subscribe_functions"}),
        entries=(
            EntrySchema(
                "subscribe_functions",
                frozenset({"fn_name", "topic_arg_index", "handler_arg_index"}),
                required=("fn_name",),
            ),
        ),
    ),
}

## DERIVED, and refused with a reason rather than reported as unknown. `key_alias_prefixes`
## is resolved FROM the shared-key document plus the tier-4 ecosystem defaults, so accepting
## a stated value here would let it disagree with the patterns it is supposed to describe.
## Naming it explicitly matters: "unknown option" would send a caller looking for a typo in
## a key that is spelled correctly and simply is not theirs to set.
DERIVED_OPTIONS: dict[str, str] = {
    "key_alias_prefixes": (
        "derived from shared_key_patterns plus the built-in ecosystem prefixes — state "
        "shared_key_patterns instead, and read the resolved value back from "
        "status.options"
    ),
}

## The roles `event_tags` may assign. Imported from the importer that consumes them rather
## than restated, so a role this accepts is a role something reads.
EVENT_ROLES: frozenset[str] = frozenset({PRODUCER, CONSUMER})


## @brief Raised when an options mapping names something unknown or is shaped wrongly.
## @version 1
class BuildOptionError(ValueError):
    """A REFUSAL, not a warning. An option that is silently dropped produces a build whose
    policy is not what the caller stated and which reports success — the failure mode this
    whole surface exists to remove, reintroduced at its own front door.

    @brief Invalid build options.
    @version 1
    """


## @brief Every option key this surface accepts, for an error message and for a caller.
## @return Sorted tuple of accepted key names.
## @version 3
## @req REQ-DDB-CONFIG-008
def accepted_options() -> tuple[str, ...]:
    """@brief The accepted option names.

    @return Sorted key names.
    @version 2
    """
    return tuple(
        sorted(
            (
                *INLINE_LIST_OPTIONS,
                *INLINE_MAPPING_OPTIONS,
                *PATH_OPTIONS,
                *MANIFEST_OPTIONS,
                *SECTION_DOCUMENT_OPTIONS,
            )
        )
    )


## @brief Refuse a key that is not settable, naming why.
## @param key The offending option name.
## @return None; always raises.
## @version 1
## @dg_internal
def _refuse(key: str) -> None:
    """Split from the validation loop so the DERIVED case gets its own sentence. Reporting
    a correctly-spelled derived key as "unknown" is worse than useless — it sends the reader
    hunting a typo that is not there, which is this repo's recorded phantom-hunt shape.

    @brief Raise the right refusal for an unsettable key.
    @version 1
    """
    if key in DERIVED_OPTIONS:
        raise BuildOptionError(f"option {key!r} cannot be stated: {DERIVED_OPTIONS[key]}")
    raise BuildOptionError(
        f"unknown build option {key!r} — accepted: {', '.join(accepted_options())}"
    )


## @brief Validate one inline mapping option's entries.
## @param key The option name, for the message.
## @param value The mapping supplied.
## @return The mapping, unchanged, when every entry is valid.
## @version 1
## @dg_internal
def _checked_mapping(key: str, value: Any) -> dict[str, str]:
    """THE ENTRY-LEVEL GATE, and the reason it exists is that this level is the quiet one.
    A document-level slip is loud; `{"broadcasts": "produce"}` is a valid mapping that no

## @param key The option name, for the message.
## @param value The list supplied.
## @return The list as strings.
## @version 1
## @dg_internal
def _checked_list(key: str, value: Any) -> list[str]:
    """A bare string is the likely slip and is refused rather than accepted as a
    one-character-per-item list, which is what `list("app_main")` would silently produce.

    @brief Check an inline list option.
    @return The validated list.
    @version 1
    """
    if isinstance(value, str) or not isinstance(value, (list, tuple)):
        raise BuildOptionError(
            f"option {key!r} must be a list of strings, got {type(value).__name__}"
        )
    return [str(item) for item in value]


## @brief Validate a stated declaration SECTION document.
## @param key The option/section name, for the message.
## @param value The document supplied.
## @return The document, unchanged.
## @version 1
## @dg_internal
def _checked_section_document(key: str, value: Any) -> dict:
    """A MAPPING AND NOTHING MORE, deliberately, and it is NOT `_checked_mapping`. That one
    is the `event_tags` validator: it requires every value to be an event ROLE and refuses an
    empty document. Reusing it here raised `TypeError: unhashable type: 'list'` on a perfectly
    valid `preprocessor: {predefined: [...]}` — a validator borrowed for a shape it was never
    written for, which is the same family as one option taking another's decoder.

    THE SECTION'S OWN LOADER POLICES ITS KEYS. `load_declaration_located` refuses an unknown
    section by name, and each reader validates its own entries — `preprocessor` its macro
    list and config header, `kconfig` its path. A second validator here would give one
    document two authorities free to disagree, and the entry level is exactly where a
    silent slip (`key_arg_idx` for `key_arg_index`) does its damage.

    AN EMPTY DOCUMENT IS ALLOWED because `{}` is the withdrawal spelling every other option
    uses. `_checked_mapping` rejects it, which would have made a stated section impossible to
    retract without deleting the database.

    @brief Check that a stated section is a mapping.
    @return The document.
    @version 1
    """
    if not isinstance(value, dict):
        raise BuildOptionError(
            f"option {key!r} states the whole `{key}:` declaration section, so it must be a "
            f"mapping, got {type(value).__name__}"
        )

## @brief Resolve one path option against the repo root.
## @param key The option name, for the message.
## @param value The path supplied.
## @param repo_root Root to resolve a relative path against, or None.
## @return Absolute path as a string.
## @version 2
## @dg_internal
def _checked_path(key: str, value: Any, repo_root: Path | None) -> str:
    """Relative paths resolve against the REPO, not the process's working directory: a
    caller states the path they would write in the declaration file, and an MCP server's
    cwd is not the target repo. Existence is NOT checked for most of them — each loader
    reports its own missing document with the context to say what it was for.

    THE EXCEPTION IS `PATH_OPTIONS_MUST_EXIST`, and the line the exception is drawn on is
    metadata versus file set. A missing `requirements` catalog degrades to empty metadata over
    the same rows, so the loader's own message is both sufficient and better-informed. A missing
    `doxyfile` sends resolution through to whole-repo synthesis, which is a LEGITIMATE build —
    so there is no loader left to complain, and the result is a well-formed index of a different
    variant of the repository, reporting success.

    @brief Resolve a path option.
    @return Absolute path string.
    @version 2
    """
    if not isinstance(value, (str, Path)):
        raise BuildOptionError(
            f"option {key!r} must be a path to a YAML document, got {type(value).__name__}"
        )

    if not path.is_absolute() and repo_root is not None:
        path = Path(repo_root) / path
    if key in PATH_OPTIONS_MUST_EXIST and not path.is_file():
        raise BuildOptionError(
            f"option {key!r} names {path}, which is not a file. Refusing rather than "
            f"continuing: this option decides WHICH SOURCE is indexed, so falling back "
            f"would build a well-formed index of something else and report success. "
            f"State a path relative to the repo root, or remove the option to let "
            f"discovery and synthesis decide."
        )
    return str(path)


## @brief Validate one inline manifest document against its schema.
## @param key The option name, for the message.
## @param value The mapping supplied.
## @return The mapping, unchanged, when the whole document is valid.
## @version 1
## @dg_internal
def _checked_document(key: str, value: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """The DOCUMENT half of the two-level gate. A manifest with no schema here is one whose
    own loader refuses unknown keys at both levels (`dispatch`), so it passes through — but
    it passes through NAMED, rather than by falling off the end of a lookup, because "no
    schema" and "not checked" must not share a code path.

    @brief Check an inline manifest's top-level keys.
    @return The validated document.
    @version 1
    """
    schema = MANIFEST_SCHEMAS.get(key)
    if schema is None:
        return value  # dispatch: validated wholly by load_dispatch_manifest
    unknown = sorted(str(k) for k in value if k not in schema.document)
    if unknown:
        raise BuildOptionError(
            f"option {key!r} names unknown key(s) {', '.join(repr(k) for k in unknown)} "
            f"— allowed: {', '.join(sorted(schema.document))}. Nothing reads an unknown "
            f"key, so the build would have used built-in defaults while reporting that "
            f"your statement was honoured."

## @param key The option name, for the message.
## @param document The manifest document.
## @param schema The entry schema for one of its lists.
## @return None; raises on the first offending entry.
## @version 1
## @dg_internal
def _checked_entries(key: str, document: dict[str, Any], schema: EntrySchema) -> None:
    """THE QUIET LEVEL, and the whole reason the inline route is validated harder than the
    file route. `key_arg_idx` for `key_arg_index` is a valid mapping that every loader reads
    as "absent", so the dataflow is keyed off argument 0 and the build reports success —
    this repo's recorded example of an entry-level slip. Same family as
    `entry.get("name")` returning None and the loader skipping the entry silently.

    @brief Check one manifest list's entries.
    @version 1

    entries = document.get(schema.list_key)
    if entries is None:
        return
    if not isinstance(entries, list):
        raise BuildOptionError(
            f"option {key!r}: {schema.list_key!r} must be a list of entries, got "
            f"{type(entries).__name__}"

        _checked_entry(key, f"{schema.list_key}[{position}]", entry, schema)


## @brief Validate one entry mapping against its schema.
## @param key The option name, for the message.
## @param where Which list and position the entry sits at.
## @param entry The entry supplied.
## @param schema The entry schema.
## @return None; raises when the entry is shaped wrongly.
## @version 1
## @dg_internal
def _checked_entry(key: str, where: str, entry: Any, schema: EntrySchema) -> None:
    """@brief Check one manifest entry's keys against the allowed and required sets.
    @version 1
    """
    if not isinstance(entry, dict):
        raise BuildOptionError(
            f"option {key!r}: {where} must be a mapping, got {type(entry).__name__}"
        )
    unknown = sorted(str(k) for k in entry if k not in schema.allowed)
    if unknown:
        raise BuildOptionError(
            f"option {key!r}: {where} names unknown key(s) "
            f"{', '.join(repr(k) for k in unknown)} — allowed: "
            f"{', '.join(sorted(schema.allowed))}. A misspelled field reads as an absent "
            f"one, so it would silently take its default."
        )
    missing = [name for name in schema.required if not entry.get(name)]
    if missing:
        raise BuildOptionError(
            f"option {key!r}: {where} is missing required key(s) "
            f"{', '.join(repr(m) for m in missing)}"
        )
    if schema.any_of and not any(entry.get(name) for name in schema.any_of):
        raise BuildOptionError(
            f"option {key!r}: {where} declares none of "
            f"{', '.join(repr(name) for name in schema.any_of)} — it would match nothing"
        )

## @param key The option name, for the message.
## @param value A path string/Path, or the manifest document as a mapping.
## @param repo_root Root to resolve a relative path against, or None.
## @return An absolute path string, or the validated mapping.
## @version 1
## @dg_internal
def _checked_manifest(key: str, value: Any, repo_root: Path | None) -> str | dict[str, Any]:
    """BOTH FORMS REACH THE SAME PARSER. Every loader behind these options already accepts
    `Path | dict`, because a `.doxyguard-db.yaml` section arrives as a mapping — so the
    inline form adds a route, not a format, and `treescan.manifest_key` hashes a mapping
    canonically, which is what keeps gh#358's per-stage cache invalidation intact: stating
    one manifest recomputes the stages that manifest feeds and no others.

    @brief Resolve a manifest option from either input form.
    @return Path string or validated document.
    @version 1
    """
    if isinstance(value, dict):
        return _checked_document(key, value)
    if not isinstance(value, (str, Path)):
        raise BuildOptionError(
            f"option {key!r} must be a path to a YAML document, or that document inline "
            f"as a mapping, got {type(value).__name__}"
        )
    return _checked_path(key, value, repo_root)


## @brief Apply a validated options mapping onto a parsed argument namespace.
## @param args Namespace from the build argument parser, mutated in place.
## @param options Caller-stated options, or None to change nothing.
## @param repo_root Root that relative path options resolve against.
## @return The names actually applied, sorted, for logging.
## @version 3
## @req REQ-DDB-CONFIG-008
def apply_options(args: Any, options: dict[str, Any] | None, repo_root: Path | None) -> list[str]:
    """VALIDATES EVERYTHING BEFORE ASSIGNING ANYTHING, so a mapping with one bad entry
    leaves the namespace untouched rather than half-applied. A partially-applied policy
    would build with a mixture of what the caller asked for and what they did not, and
    report success — the same class of defect as a partially-reloaded pipeline.

    `None` and `{}` both change nothing, and neither is an error: a caller that forwards
    its own optional argument gets the inheriting behaviour by default. An empty document
    for ONE manifest option (`shared_key_patterns: {}`) is the per-option equivalent — it
    states nothing, so that manifest falls back to the target's own declaration, matching
    the absent/empty/replaces convention `--exclude` and `--entry-patterns` already keep.

    @brief Validate and apply tier-1 options.
    @return Applied option names.
    @version 2
    """
    if not options:
        return []
    if not isinstance(options, dict):
        raise BuildOptionError(f"options must be a mapping, got {type(options).__name__}")
    staged: dict[str, Any] = {}
    for key, value in options.items():
        if key in INLINE_LIST_OPTIONS:
            staged[key] = _checked_list(key, value)
        elif key in INLINE_MAPPING_OPTIONS:
            staged[key] = _checked_mapping(key, value)
        elif key in MANIFEST_OPTIONS:
            staged[key] = _checked_manifest(key, value, repo_root)
        elif key in PATH_OPTIONS:
            staged[key] = _checked_path(key, value, repo_root)
        elif key in SECTION_DOCUMENT_OPTIONS:
            staged[key] = _checked_section_document(key, value)
        else:
            _refuse(key)
    for key, value in staged.items():
        setattr(args, key, value)
    return sorted(staged)

1	# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
2	"""Five-tier precedence for every layered build option — ONE combination rule.
3	
4	`resolved = (tier1 or tier2 or tier5) union tier3 union tier4`
5	
6	In one line: **you can correct our guesses; you cannot un-discover a fact.**
7	
8	| tier | name | what it is | combines by |
9	|---|---|---|---|
10	| 1 | explicit | a CLI flag | REPLACES the stated layer |
11	| 2 | declared | `.doxyguard-db.yaml` / the `x-doxyguard-db` passthrough | REPLACES the stated layer |
12	| 3 | target-fact | facts someone else already wrote — a Doxyfile's ALIASES/PREDEFINED, a generator manifest, a language or platform entry point | ACCUMULATES |
13	| 4 | ecosystem | a known-ecosystem signature (UDM, ingot) | ACCUMULATES |
14	| 5 | heuristic | name-pattern matching; the floor, explicitly provisional | REPLACES the stated layer |
15	
16	WHY THIS MODULE EXISTS. "Supersede" meant three different things across the
17	pipeline, so moving one value from a declaration to a flag silently changed
18	behaviour: `cli._entry_patterns` had the flag REPLACE and the declaration EXTEND;
19	`shared_key_edges` had the declaration REPLACE; `--extra-input` APPENDS. The
20	collapse that motivated the work: passing `--entry-patterns` dropped `main`,
21	reachability collapsed, and NOTHING reported it. Under this rule a stated tier
22	can only displace the guesses, so `main` survives whatever anyone states.
23	
24	TIERS 3 AND 4 HAVE IDENTICAL COMBINATION BEHAVIOUR, and saying so is the point
25	rather than an omission. Both accumulate and both survive every stated tier, so
26	an arguable 3-vs-4 call is inert — it changes the label a reader sees and nothing
27	about the resolved set. The load-bearing distinction is 3-or-4 versus 5: calling
28	a fact a guess makes it discardable, and calling a guess a fact makes it
29	permanent. Spend the argument there.
30	
31	NOT IN `vocabulary.py`, deliberately. That module's contract is an enumerated
32	COLUMN's allowed values: a `Vocabulary` carries members, meaning and rank so the
33	DDL can ask it for a constraint clause, and a test scans the package to prove the
34	literal spelling of that clause appears in no other file. A tier is not a column —
35	the winning tier is stored in `build_meta`, whose schema is
36	`(key TEXT PRIMARY KEY, value TEXT)`, so there is no clause here to generate.
37	Forcing it in would put a value set there that nothing can generate one for, which
38	is how that file starts becoming "constants". This module takes the same LEAF
39	discipline instead: `dataclasses` and `collections.abc`, no intra-package imports,
40	so `signature.py` can import it without acquiring `rich`.
41	
42	(That scan is not a hypothetical: the first draft of this docstring quoted the
43	clause keyword verbatim while explaining why the module does not use it, and the
44	test failed. A gate that reads text cannot tell an example from a usage.)
45	
46	@brief Tiered precedence and the single layered-option resolution primitive.
47	@version 1
48	"""
49	
50	from __future__ import annotations
51	
52	import json
53	from collections.abc import Iterable, Mapping, Sequence
54	from dataclasses import dataclass
55	from typing import Any
56	
57	## Tier 1 — an operator's explicit CLI flag for this one build.
58	TIER_EXPLICIT = "explicit"
59	## Tier 2 — the target repo's standing declaration.
60	TIER_DECLARED = "declared"
61	## Tier 3 — a fact someone else already wrote down (language, platform, or the
62	## target's own manifests). Accumulates; no stated tier can remove it.
63	TIER_TARGET_FACT = "target-fact"
64	## Tier 4 — a known-ecosystem signature. Accumulates, exactly as tier 3 does.
65	TIER_ECOSYSTEM = "ecosystem"
66	## Tier 5 — a name-pattern guess. The floor, and the only built-in layer a stated
67	## tier is allowed to displace.
68	TIER_HEURISTIC = "heuristic"
69	
70	## Highest precedence first. Used for reporting and for pinning the tier names in
71	## one place; the combination rule below is not derived from position, because
72	## tiers 3 and 4 do not participate in precedence at all.
73	TIER_ORDER: tuple[str, ...] = (
74	    TIER_EXPLICIT,
75	    TIER_DECLARED,
76	    TIER_TARGET_FACT,
77	    TIER_ECOSYSTEM,
78	    TIER_HEURISTIC,
79	)
80	
81	## The three tiers that compete to supply the REPLACEABLE layer, highest first.
82	STATED_TIERS: tuple[str, ...] = (TIER_EXPLICIT, TIER_DECLARED, TIER_HEURISTIC)
83	
84	## The two tiers that accumulate underneath and survive every stated tier.
85	ACCUMULATING_TIERS: tuple[str, ...] = (TIER_TARGET_FACT, TIER_ECOSYSTEM)
86	
87	## The `build_meta` prefix the resolved options are stamped under, imported by
88	## both the writer (`signature`) and the reader (`cli`) rather than spelled twice.
89	## The four older sections still carry their prefix as a literal in both places;
90	## that duplication predates this constant and churning it is unrelated work.
91	OPTIONS_META_PREFIX = "options"
92	
93	## Per-option keys inside that section.
94	TIER_KEY = "tier"
95	EXPLICIT_KEY = "explicit"
96	
97	## How a stored DOCUMENT is serialised: sorted keys and no whitespace, i.e. CANONICAL.
98	## Byte-stability across processes is the requirement, not compactness. A manifest
99	## document arrives as a mapping whose insertion order is whatever the caller (or a YAML
100	## parser) happened to produce, so an unsorted dump of two equal documents differs by
101	## bytes — and `build_meta` is compared verbatim by
102	## `test_warm_rebuild_is_deterministic`, which would then fail intermittently rather
103	## than usefully. Sorting also means a re-stated identical document produces an
104	## identical row, so nothing downstream sees a change where none was made.
105	DOCUMENT_SEPARATORS: tuple[str, str] = (",", ":")
106	
107	## How a stored value LIST is joined. A NEWLINE, not `scope.py`'s `", "`, and the
108	## difference is load-bearing rather than stylistic: the values here are SQL LIKE
109	## patterns and a pattern containing a comma or a space (`handle,%`, `on %`) is
110	## perfectly ordinary, while one containing a newline is not something a shell
111	## invocation produces. `scope`'s separator is safe for the repo-relative PATHS it
112	## joins and would corrupt the replay here.
113	VALUE_SEPARATOR = "\n"
114	
115	
116	## @brief One layered option's resolved values together with the tier that won.
117	## @version 1
118	@dataclass(frozen=True)
119	class LayeredResolution:
120	    """The values AND their provenance, bound together so a caller cannot hold one
121	    without the other.
122	
123	    That binding is the mechanism, not decoration. The task this implements states
124	    that a tiered resolution is only useful if the tier that won is recorded and
125	    reported — otherwise it is the same opacity with more steps. A resolver
126	    returning a bare list makes forgetting the default; returning this makes
127	    forgetting require deliberately discarding a field, and `options_meta` below
128	    REFUSES anything that is not one of these, so the stamping path cannot be fed
129	    values whose tier was dropped along the way.
130	
131	    `stated` is the winning stated layer verbatim, kept apart from `values`
132	    because only a tier-1 statement is ever replayed onto a later build — a tier-2
133	    declaration re-derives itself from a file that may have changed since, and
134	    replaying a stored copy would freeze a stale declaration.
135	
136	    @brief A resolved layered option: values, winning tier, stated layer.
137	    @version 1
138	    """
139	
140	    values: tuple[str, ...]
141	    tier: str
142	    stated: tuple[str, ...]
143	
144	    ## @brief Flatten this resolution into `build_meta` rows for one option.
145	    ## @param option The option's name, used as the key prefix inside the section.
146	    ## @return Mapping of unprefixed build_meta key to value.
147	    ## @version 1
148	    ## @req REQ-DDB-CONFIG-006
149	    def as_meta(self, option: str) -> dict[str, str]:
150	        """The tier is ALWAYS recorded; the stated layer only when tier 1 won.
151	
152	        Writing `explicit` unconditionally would make the read-back replay a
153	        declaration or the built-in guesses as though an operator had typed them,
154	        which is the failure `_operator_excludes` avoids by recording only what the
155	        operator actually stated. An absent key honestly reads as "nothing to
156	        replay", matching the writer's rule that falsy values are dropped.
157	
158	        @brief Build the build_meta fragment for this resolution.
159	        @return Unprefixed key/value mapping.
160	        @version 1
161	        """
162	        meta = {f"{option}.{TIER_KEY}": self.tier}
163	        if self.tier == TIER_EXPLICIT and self.stated:
164	            meta[f"{option}.{EXPLICIT_KEY}"] = VALUE_SEPARATOR.join(self.stated)
165	        return meta
166	
167	
168	## @brief Serialise a stated document to the byte-stable form `build_meta` stores.
169	## @param value The stated document, or the path string that names one.
170	## @return Canonical JSON: sorted keys, no whitespace.
171	## @version 1
172	## @req REQ-DDB-CONFIG-006
173	def canonical_document(value: str | Mapping[str, Any]) -> str:
174	    """CANONICAL MEANS BYTE-STABLE ACROSS PROCESSES, and that is a correctness
175	    property here rather than tidiness. Two builds of one unchanged tree must produce
176	    an identical `build_meta`, which is what `test_warm_rebuild_is_deterministic`
177	    asserts; a dump that preserved insertion order would make the stored row a
178	    function of how the caller happened to spell its mapping, so re-stating an
179	    equal document would read as a change.
180	
181	    A PATH and a DOCUMENT share this one row and JSON tells them apart for free — a
182	    path serialises as a JSON string, a document as a JSON object — so the reader
183	    needs no second key to say which form was stated, and cannot get that answer
184	    wrong.
185	
186	    @brief Canonically serialise a stated manifest document or path.
187	    @return The stored representation.
188	    @version 1
189	    """
190	    return json.dumps(value, sort_keys=True, separators=DOCUMENT_SEPARATORS)
191	
192	
193	## @brief One manifest-shaped option's stated document together with the tier that supplied it.
194	## @version 1
195	@dataclass(frozen=True)
196	class DocumentResolution:
197	    """THE DOCUMENT COUNTERPART of `LayeredResolution`, for the five manifest options
198	    whose stated layer is a whole document (or a path to one) rather than a list of
199	    strings — `shared_key_patterns`, `thread_patterns`, `locks`, `dispatch`,
200	    `mqtt_dispatch`.
201	
202	    IT CARRIES NO `values`, deliberately. A manifest's resolved effect is rows in a
203	    dozen tables, computed several frames down inside the loaders; there is no short
204	    value to record and inventing one would put a summary in `build_meta` that the
205	    tables are free to disagree with. What is recordable — and what a later build
206	    needs — is WHO supplied the document and, when that was an operator, the document
207	    itself.
208	
209	    WHY THE STAMP IS LOAD-BEARING AND NOT DECORATION (owner decision, gh#364).
210	    Replaying a statement means the index carries a policy the REPOSITORY does not
211	    declare, so two operators of the same commit can get different indexes. That is
212	    the shape of the defect rejected in gh#352, where an external tag was a property
213	    of the working COPY rather than of the repository. What makes it acceptable here
214	    is that a statement is DELIBERATE and RECORDED where the gitlink case was
215	    accidental and silent. If this row is missing, this becomes that defect. Two
216	    operators may differ; they must never differ SILENTLY.
217	
218	    @brief A resolved manifest option: the winning tier and the stated document.
219	    @version 1
220	    """
221	
222	    tier: str
223	    stated: str | Mapping[str, Any] | None = None
224	
225	    ## @brief Flatten this resolution into `build_meta` rows for one option.
226	    ## @param option The option's name, used as the key prefix inside the section.
227	    ## @return Mapping of unprefixed build_meta key to value.
228	    ## @version 1
229	    ## @req REQ-DDB-CONFIG-006
230	    def as_meta(self, option: str) -> dict[str, str]:
231	        """THE TIER IS ALWAYS WRITTEN, exactly as `LayeredResolution.as_meta` writes
232	        it, and for the reason `recorded_explicit` documents: the tier row is what
233	        makes a withdrawal unreplayable. `write_build_signature` upserts and never
234	        deletes, so a retracted statement can survive beside a fresh tier row, and the
235	        reader resolves that contradiction by trusting the tier. Skip the tier row for
236	        a withdrawal and that guard has nothing to compare against.
237	
238	        The DOCUMENT is written only for a tier-1 win. A tier-2 declaration re-derives
239	        itself from a file that may have changed since, so replaying a stored copy
240	        would freeze a stale declaration.
241	
242	        @brief Build the build_meta fragment for this resolution.
243	        @return Unprefixed key/value mapping.
244	        @version 1
245	        """
246	        meta = {f"{option}.{TIER_KEY}": self.tier}
247	        if self.tier == TIER_EXPLICIT and self.stated:
248	            meta[f"{option}.{EXPLICIT_KEY}"] = canonical_document(self.stated)
249	        return meta
250	
251	
252	## @brief Resolve one manifest option: an operator's statement, else the declaration.
253	## @param explicit Tier-1 statement — a path string, the document inline, or falsy.
254	## @param declared The target's own declared document, or falsy when it declares none.
255	## @return The resolution, carrying the winning tier and the statement to record.
256	## @version 1
257	## @req REQ-DDB-CONFIG-006
258	def resolve_document(
259	    *,
260	    explicit: str | Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
261	    declared: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
262	) -> DocumentResolution:
263	    """THE SAME THREE-WAY CHOICE `_stated_layer` makes, on a document instead of a
264	    list, so `cli._declared_or_flag`'s precedence and this label cannot disagree about
265	    which tier won.
266	
267	    AN EMPTY DOCUMENT IS A WITHDRAWAL, not a statement — `{}` is falsy, so it falls
268	    through to the declaration and then to the floor, and no statement is recorded.
269	    That is one spelling doing both jobs on purpose (owner decision, gh#364): clearing
270	    an option means "stop overriding", which is the same intent as "fall back to the
271	    target's own declaration".
272	
273	    THE FLOOR IS LABELLED `heuristic` AND THAT NEEDS READING CAREFULLY. It does NOT
274	    say the built-in lock, spawn and accessor patterns are guesses — those are tier-3
275	    and tier-4 layers that ACCUMULATE underneath and no stated tier can displace them.
276	    It says nobody stated a document, so the replaceable layer is empty and the
277	    resolved set is exactly what accumulates. That is the identical meaning
278	    `_stated_layer` gives the label when no list is stated either.
279	
280	    @brief Resolve which tier supplied one manifest document.
281	    @return The resolution for that option.
282	    @version 1
283	    """
284	    if explicit:
285	        return DocumentResolution(TIER_EXPLICIT, explicit)
286	    if declared:
287	        return DocumentResolution(TIER_DECLARED)
288	    return DocumentResolution(TIER_HEURISTIC)
289	
290	
291	## @brief Resolve one layered option: (tier1 or tier2 or tier5) union tier3 union tier4.
292	## @param facts Tier-3 values — facts someone else already wrote. Always present.
293	## @param explicit Tier-1 values from a CLI flag; None absent, [] withdrawn.
294	## @param declared Tier-2 values from the target's declaration, or None.
295	## @param ecosystem Tier-4 values from a known-ecosystem signature.
296	## @param heuristics Tier-5 name-pattern guesses — the layer a stated tier displaces.
297	## @return The resolved values and the stated tier that won.
298	## @version 1
299	## @req REQ-DDB-CONFIG-006
300	def resolve_layered(
301	    *,
302	    facts: Iterable[str],
303	    explicit: Sequence[str] | None = None,
304	    declared: Sequence[str] | None = None,
305	    ecosystem: Iterable[str] = (),
306	    heuristics: Iterable[str] = (),
307	) -> LayeredResolution:
308	    """KEYWORD-ONLY, because five same-typed sequence arguments in a row is a
309	    transposition waiting to happen and transposing `facts` with `heuristics` would
310	    invert the whole rule silently — the accumulating layer would become
311	    discardable and the guesses would become permanent, with every count still
312	    looking legitimate.
313	
314	    THE ACCUMULATING LAYERS COME FIRST in the resolved order, so a target that
315	    states nothing resolves to exactly `(*facts, *ecosystem, *heuristics)` — the
316	    built-in default set, unchanged and comparable by equality rather than by set
317	    membership. That makes the success-path control a strict assertion instead of a
318	    loose one, which matters here: this repo has shipped a check that tested only
319	    its failure path.
320	
321	    AN EMPTY `explicit` IS A WITHDRAWAL, not a statement. `[]` is falsy, so it
322	    falls through to the declaration and then to the guesses, which is what lets an
323	    operator undo a recorded flag without deleting the database. `None` means the
324	    flag was absent.
325	
326	    @brief Combine the five tiers into one resolved option.
327	    @return The resolution, carrying the winning stated tier.
328	    @version 1
329	    """
330	    tier, stated = _stated_layer(explicit, declared, heuristics)
331	    return LayeredResolution(
332	        values=_ordered_unique((*facts, *ecosystem, *stated)),
333	        tier=tier,
334	        stated=stated,
335	    )
336	
337	
338	## @brief Pick the stated layer: tier 1, else tier 2, else the tier-5 floor.
339	## @param explicit Tier-1 values, or None.
340	## @param declared Tier-2 values, or None.
341	## @param heuristics Tier-5 values.
342	## @return (winning tier name, that tier's values).
343	## @version 1
344	## @dg_internal
345	def _stated_layer(
346	    explicit: Sequence[str] | None,
347	    declared: Sequence[str] | None,
348	    heuristics: Iterable[str],
349	) -> tuple[str, tuple[str, ...]]:
350	    """@brief Choose which of the three replaceable tiers supplies the stated layer.
351	    @return The tier name and its values.
352	    @version 1
353	    """
354	    if explicit:
355	        return TIER_EXPLICIT, tuple(str(v) for v in explicit)
356	    if declared:
357	        return TIER_DECLARED, tuple(str(v) for v in declared)
358	    return TIER_HEURISTIC, tuple(heuristics)
359	
360	
361	## @brief De-duplicate while preserving first-seen order.
362	## @param values The concatenated layers.
363	## @return Order-preserving unique tuple.
364	## @version 1
365	## @dg_internal
366	def _ordered_unique(values: Iterable[str]) -> tuple[str, ...]:
367	    """A stated tier may legitimately restate a fact (`--entry-patterns main …`),
368	    and a duplicated SQL LIKE pattern would add a redundant `OR name LIKE ?` term
369	    rather than break anything — but the stored provenance and the reported set
370	    would both show it, so it is removed here once instead of at each consumer.
371	
372	    @brief Remove duplicates, keeping the first occurrence.
373	    @return Unique values in order.
374	    @version 1
375	    """
376	    seen: dict[str, None] = {}
377	    for value in values:
378	        seen.setdefault(value, None)
379	    return tuple(seen)
380	
381	
382	## The two resolution types the stamping path accepts — a list-valued option and a
383	## document-valued one. A TUPLE rather than a widened `isinstance` written inline,
384	## because the REFUSAL is the mechanism: adding a third resolution type must be a
385	## deliberate edit here, and a bare list or mapping must keep being rejected.
386	RESOLUTION_TYPES: tuple[type, ...] = (LayeredResolution, DocumentResolution)
387	
388	
389	## @brief Flatten resolved options into the `build_meta` section they are stamped as.
390	## @param resolutions Option name to its LayeredResolution or DocumentResolution.
391	## @return Unprefixed build_meta mapping covering every option given.
392	## @version 2
393	## @req REQ-DDB-CONFIG-006
394	def options_meta(**resolutions: LayeredResolution | DocumentResolution) -> dict[str, str]:
395	    """THE ONLY PRODUCER of the `options.*` rows, and it accepts only resolutions.
396	
397	    That refusal is what makes "record the tier" structural rather than a habit. A
398	    caller cannot stamp a layered option from a bare list, because there is no code
399	    path from a list to these rows; it has to hold the object that knows which tier
400	    won. Raising `TypeError` rather than coercing follows the repo's fail-closed
401	    rule — a silently skipped option would present exactly as an older index that
402	    never recorded one.
403	
404	    A DOCUMENT-VALUED OPTION goes through the same door (gh#364). The five manifest
405	    options state a whole document rather than a list, and routing them through a
406	    second producer would give the `options.*` section two writers free to disagree
407	    about the key layout the reader depends on.
408	
409	    @brief Build the `options` build_meta section from resolutions.
410	    @return Unprefixed key/value mapping.
411	    @version 2
412	    """
413	    meta: dict[str, str] = {}
414	    for option, resolution in resolutions.items():
415	        if not isinstance(resolution, RESOLUTION_TYPES):
416	            raise TypeError(
417	                f"options_meta({option}=...) needs a LayeredResolution or "
418	                f"DocumentResolution carrying its winning tier, got "
419	                f"{type(resolution).__name__}. Resolve the option through "
420	                f"resolve_layered() or resolve_document() rather than passing bare values."
421	            )
422	        meta.update(resolution.as_meta(option))
423	    return meta
424	
425	
426	## @brief Read back the tier-1 statement a previous build recorded for one option.
427	## @param section The prefix-stripped `options` build_meta section.
428	## @param option The option's name.
429	## @return The recorded explicit values, or () when none was recorded or the tier disagrees.
430	## @version 2
431	## @req REQ-DDB-CONFIG-006
432	def recorded_explicit(section: Mapping[str, str], option: str) -> tuple[str, ...]:
433	    """ONLY tier 1 is replayable, and this CROSS-CHECKS the tier rather than
434	    trusting the statement key alone.
435	
436	    The first version read the statement key by itself, on the argument that the
437	    policy lived in the writer so the reader had no decision to get wrong. A
438	    control written in the awkward direction — stamp an explicit statement, then
439	    stamp its WITHDRAWAL onto the same database — showed that wrong.
440	    `write_build_signature` upserts and never deletes, so the retracted
441	    `<option>.explicit` row survived beside a fresh `<option>.tier = heuristic` and
442	    this function replayed a statement the operator had just withdrawn.
443	
444	    The real pipeline does not reach it today, because every build stamps a fresh
445	    temp database that then replaces the live one — but that is an invariant in a
446	    DIFFERENT module, and depending on it silently means a later caller stamping
447	    onto a live database (which `_stamp_refresh_metrics` already does, for another
448	    section) turns a retraction into a replay with nothing to notice it.
449	
450	    So the TIER is authoritative: it is written on every stamp, and a statement
451	    that disagrees with it is a contradictory record, which resolves to "nothing to
452	    replay" rather than to the more interesting of the two readings.
453	
454	    Same defect this closes as `_operator_excludes`: a resolution that is applied
455	    and recorded but never read back is discarded by the next refresh, which then
456	    reports success over exactly the shape the operator asked for.
457	
458	    @brief Read one option's recorded explicit statement, if the tier agrees.
459	    @return The recorded values, or ().
460	    @version 2
461	    """
462	    if section.get(f"{option}.{TIER_KEY}") != TIER_EXPLICIT:
463	        return ()
464	    raw = section.get(f"{option}.{EXPLICIT_KEY}", "")
465	    return tuple(part for part in raw.split(VALUE_SEPARATOR) if part)
466	
467	
468	## @brief Read back the tier-1 manifest DOCUMENT a previous build recorded for one option.
469	## @param section The prefix-stripped `options` build_meta section.
470	## @param option The option's name.
471	## @return The recorded document or path, or None when none was recorded or the tier disagrees.
472	## @version 1
473	## @req REQ-DDB-CONFIG-006
474	def recorded_document(section: Mapping[str, str], option: str) -> str | dict[str, Any] | None:
475	    """THE SAME TIER CROSS-CHECK `recorded_explicit` DOES, and it is checked here for
476	    the document form rather than assumed to carry over: the guard lives in the READER,
477	    so a second reader that skipped it would replay a withdrawn statement while the
478	    first one refused to. `write_build_signature` upserts and never deletes, so a
479	    retracted `<option>.explicit` row can outlive the statement it recorded; the tier
480	    row is written on every stamp, so the tier is authoritative and a statement that
481	    disagrees with it resolves to "nothing to replay".
482	
483	    A CORRUPT RECORD RAISES rather than reading as "no statement". Reverting silently
484	    to the target's own declaration is precisely the defect this whole read-back
485	    exists to remove — a build that cannot honour the recorded policy must not report
486	    success over a different one. Nothing but this module writes the row, so reaching
487	    the raise means the database was edited by hand.
488	
489	    @brief Read one option's recorded manifest statement, if the tier agrees.
490	    @return The recorded document, the recorded path, or None.
491	    @version 1
492	    """
493	    if section.get(f"{option}.{TIER_KEY}") != TIER_EXPLICIT:
494	        return None
495	    raw = section.get(f"{option}.{EXPLICIT_KEY}", "")
496	    if not raw:
497	        return None
498	    return _decoded_document(option, raw)
499	
500	
501	## @brief Decode one stored document row, refusing anything that is not a path or a mapping.
502	## @param option The option's name, for the message.
503	## @param raw The stored canonical JSON.
504	## @return The path string or the document mapping.
505	## @version 1
506	## @dg_internal
507	def _decoded_document(option: str, raw: str) -> str | dict[str, Any]:
508	    """THE TYPE IS CHECKED, not just the syntax. A row decoding to a list or a number
509	    is well-formed JSON that no loader can read, and handing it on would push the
510	    failure into a manifest parser several frames away where the message would name a
511	    shape rather than a corrupt record.
512	
513	    @brief Decode and type-check a stored manifest statement.
514	    @return The decoded statement.
515	    @version 1
516	    """
517	    try:
518	        value = json.loads(raw)
519	    except ValueError as exc:  # json.JSONDecodeError is a ValueError
520	        raise ValueError(
521	            f"the recorded tier-1 statement for {option!r} is not readable ({exc}). "
522	            f"Nothing but doxyguard-db writes this row, so the index's build_meta has "
523	            f"been edited. Re-state the option, or clear it with {{}}, rather than "
524	            f"letting the build silently fall back to the target's declaration."
525	        ) from exc
526	    if not isinstance(value, (str, dict)):
527	        raise ValueError(
528	            f"the recorded tier-1 statement for {option!r} decodes to a "
529	            f"{type(value).__name__}, but a manifest statement is a path (string) or a "
530	            f"document (mapping). Re-state the option, or clear it with {{}}."
531	        )
532	    return value
533	
534	
535	## @brief Which options the index carries an operator's own statement for.
536	## @param section The prefix-stripped `options` build_meta section.
537	## @return Sorted option names whose recorded tier is tier 1.
538	## @version 1
539	## @req REQ-DDB-CONFIG-006
540	def stated_options(section: Mapping[str, str]) -> tuple[str, ...]:
541	    """THE VISIBLE STAMP, and the owner's condition for allowing a statement to be
542	    replayed at all (gh#364). A replayed statement makes this index a function of what
543	    an operator once said as well as of the commit, so two operators of one commit can
544	    legitimately hold different indexes — acceptable ONLY because it is deliberate and
545	    recorded. This is what makes it findable without reading seven option rows and
546	    knowing which tier name matters.
547	
548	    DERIVED FROM THE STORED SECTION, never stamped as a row of its own. A stored
549	    summary is a second source of truth that can disagree with the rows it summarises,
550	    which is exactly where a silent wrong answer hides — the same reason the per-target
551	    state directory was rejected as a home for the record itself.
552	
553	    @brief Name the options carrying a tier-1 statement.
554	    @return Sorted option names.
555	    @version 1
556	    """
557	    suffix = f".{TIER_KEY}"
558	    return tuple(
559	        sorted(
560	            key[: -len(suffix)]
561	            for key, value in section.items()
562	            if key.endswith(suffix) and value == TIER_EXPLICIT
563	        )
564	    )
